{{Quote|He is here. We are being held hostage. They are watching us.''"<br />"''I understand.''"<br />"''Tenth level. Thousands of battle droids.|Tion Medon, informing Obi-Wan Kenobi of General Grievous's presence on Utapau|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
'''Tion Medon''' was a [[Pau'an/Legends|Pau'an]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who served as [[Master of Port Administration]] for [[Pau City/Legends|Pau City]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]]. Holding the position for over two [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], Medon was loyal to the Republic in spite of Utapau's neutrality in that conflict. He became an unofficial leader with the arrival of [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] of the Separatists, who had his [[Droid/Legends|droids]] execute other members of the governing [[Utapaun Committee/Legends|Utapaun Committee]]. Medon served the Separatists while Utapau hosted the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]], although he secretly supported a [[Utapaun resistance|resistance movement]].

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] arrived on Utapau in search of Grievous. Medon met with the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] in Pau City, discretely confirmed that Grievous was on Utapau, and also provided an overview of the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army's]] presence. Kenobi instructed Medon to have his people take shelter and prepare any warriors for [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|battle]], and the administrator spread word of the Republic's imminent attack. Medon coordinated the resistance's collaboration with the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]], and together they were victorious against Grievous. However, the Republic forces occupied Utapau shortly afterward, and Medon was one of the first Utapauns [[Prisoner/Legends|arrested]], with his fate afterwards unknown.

==Biography==
===Early life and the Clone Wars===
[[File:TionMedon-SWCTP.png|thumb|right|300px|Tion Medon was Master of Port Administration for over two centuries.]]
Tion Medon was a [[Pau'an/Legends|Pau'an]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Homeworld/Legends|from]]<ref name="SWCE" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]<ref name="ROTS" /> [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]],<ref name="SWCE" /> [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] several [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] before the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|outbreak]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].<ref name="Birth" /> He<ref name="SWCE" /> was a [[Tion Medon's family|direct descendant]] of [[Timon Medon/Legends|Timon Medon]], who was credited with uniting the scattered nation-states and cultures on Utapau.<ref name="Databank" /> On account of his heritage, Medon served as [[Master of Port Administration]]&mdash;a [[Mayor/Legends|mayoral]]-type role<ref name="Aliens">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref>&mdash;for the [[Capital/Legends|capital]]<ref name="Locations">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> [[Pau City/Legends|Pau City]] for more than two centuries<ref name="ROTS dictionary">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> before [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places the events of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'' Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].</ref> overseeing all major traffic passing through the planet.<ref name="Databank" /> Medon maintained his ancestor's tradition of diplomatic compromise<ref name="Utapaun databank">{{DB|species|utapaun|Utapaun}}</ref> and was an influential voice in the planet's [[Utapaun Committee/Legends|governing committee]], although he was not the planetary leader.<ref name="Databank" /> The Pau'an [[Zyn Javeb]] served as one of Medon's lesser [[Aide/Legends|aides]] during the final [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="Zyn Javeb">{{CSWECite|II|142|Javeb, Zyn}}</ref>

Utapau maintained neutrality during the Clone Wars between the Republic and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> and while outwardly sharing that stance<ref name="CSWE" /> and attempting to avoid involvement in the conflict,<ref name="Fact File">{{FactFile2014|9|MED 1-2|Tion Medon}}</ref> Medon was loyal to the Republic.<ref name="CSWE" /> In the course of the war, the forces of [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], the [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander]] of the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]],<ref name="ROTS dictionary" /> arrived on Utapau, taking Medon<ref name="CSWE" /> and the entire planetary populace by surprise.<ref name="Fact File" /> Seeing their approach, Medon ordered the largely [[Utai/Legends|Utai]] crews of the [[Utapau Skyforce]]<ref name="Build the Millennium Falcon">{{BuildFalconCite|94|Starship Fact File}}</ref> and the outgunned [[Utapaun Security Forces]] [[Porax-38 starfighter]]s into hiding among the depths of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] and Utapau's concealed hangars,<ref name="Cross Sections">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> [[Sinkhole/Legends|sinkholes]], and caves,<ref name="Starship Battles">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/SBPreview6|text=''Starship Battles'' Preview 6}}</ref> concealing the planet's true military capabilities.<ref name="CSWE" />

===Captive administrator===
{{Quote|Oh, administrator, just one more thing. If I catch even the scent of a Jedi&hellip; I'll make sure this hole you live in will be swallowed by a much larger one.|General Grievous threatens Tion Medon|<ref name="Reversal" />}}
The Utapaun Committee was initially reluctant to allow the Separatists on their planet.<ref name="Fact File" /> Medon watched in horror as Grievous's<ref name="Databank" /> [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]] [[Death/Legends|executed]] the other committee members in response,<ref name="ROTS dictionary" /> making Medon the de facto planetary leader. He felt he had no choice but to lead Utapau to surrender<ref name="Fact File" /> while quietly supporting a [[Utapaun resistance|resistance movement]] in Pau City's shadowy levels.<ref name="Databank" /> The Separatists used Medon's word against his will during the occupation,<ref name="Force Collection 2">{{ForceCollection|Tion Medon|star=2}}</ref> and [[Lampay Fay/Legends|Lampay Fay]] served as his aide-de-camp during that period.<ref name="Lampay Fay">{{ForceCollection|Lampay Fay|star=1}}</ref>

[[File:Medon_and_Grievous.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Medon met with Grievous during the Separatist occupation of Utapau.]]
Near the end of the war, Grievous returned to Pau City, clutching several Pau'an hostages and claiming that they promised Medon's loyalty. The administrator greeted the general and complied with his demand to store equipment and host the members of the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]], including [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], [[Po Nudo/Legends|Po Nudo]], [[Shu Mai/Legends|Shu Mai]], [[Passel Argente/Legends|Passel Argente]], [[San Hill/Legends|San Hill]], and [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser]]. Medon promised that his new guests would be taken care of, and Grievous insisted that Utapau would remain under Separatist occupation. The general reminded Medon that any offworld communication would inhibit Grievous's "protection," and he instructed Medon to take care of the vessels that were soon to arrive. Medon complied, and before departing, Grievous grabbed Medon by the throat and threatened to destroy the sinkhole containing Pau City if he caught wind of any [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] involvement on Utapau.<ref name="Reversal" /> The Separatists established their own base in Pau City, building a factory that deliberately swallowed several ancient administrative buildings.<ref name="Fact File" />

===A Jedi's arrival===
{{Quote|Greetings, young Jedi. What brings you to our remote sanctuary?|Tion Medon to Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
In 19 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> Republic [[Clone Intelligence/Legends|clone intelligence]] intercepted a diplomatic package from the [[Chairman of Utapau/Legends|Chairman of Utapau]] that confirmed Grievous's presence on the world.<ref name="Utapau databank">{{DB|location|utapau|Utapau}}</ref> As the general had become the new Separatist [[Head of State/Legends|leader]] with the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|death]] of [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] approached Utapau in pursuit of Grievous.<ref name="ROTS" /> Medon had been ordered to reveal Grievous's presence as part of a trap,<ref name="ROTS novel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> and a number of Utapauns were to be executed if the Jedi did not leave the planet.<ref name="Ultimate Missions">''[[Ultimate Missions: Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref> Flanked by Fay, Javeb, and four other robed Pau'ans<ref name="ROTS" /> on a landing platform on the city's [[Civic Level/Legends|Civic Level]],<ref name="Locations" /> Medon approached Kenobi's [[Obi-Wan Kenobi's blue Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor/Legends|fighter]].<ref name="ROTS" /> The Jedi was surprised at the speed of their meeting, suspecting that he had been expected. Kenobi [[Force sense/Legends|sensed]] Medon's lack of malice and heightened level of fear through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and approached the administrator, who introduced himself.<ref name="ROTS novel" />

[[File:TionMedon.png|thumb|right|350px|Tion Medon meets with Obi-Wan Kenobi]]
Medon already knew of Kenobi's reputation<ref name="Fact File 39">{{FactFile2014|39|19 BBY 25-30|The Battle of Utapau}}</ref> and questioned the Jedi about his purpose on Utapau. In response to the rising anxiety he sensed in Medon, Kenobi answered truthfully and stated that the war brought him there,<ref name="ROTS novel" /> attempting to avoid mentioning Grievous as he was uncertain as to Medon's loyalties.<ref name="Fact File 39" /> The administrator feigned ignorance<ref name="Databank" /> and insisted that there was no war on Utapau, unless the Jedi brought violence with him. After Kenobi revealed that he intended to use Utapau as a staging ground to search for General Grievous in nearby [[Star system/Legends|systems]], Medon ordered three Utai mechanics to [[Fuel/Legends|refuel]] Kenobi's [[Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor/Legends|fighter]].<ref name="ROTS" /> He leaned sideways, creating the appearance of inspecting the underside of Kenobi's fighter, while blocking the view of the windows on the upper levels,<ref name="Junior">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith'' junior novel]]</ref> from which an IG-100 MagnaGuard was observing Medon and Kenobi's conversation.<ref name="ROTS" />

Hoping to secure Kenobi's aid,<ref name="Fact File" /> Medon stepped forward and whispered that Grievous was on Utapau and that his people were held hostage by the Separatists, with thousands of [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] occupying the [[Level 10/Legends|tenth level]] of the city. Kenobi instructed Medon to allow his people to take shelter and for their [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] to stand ready. The two bowed before Kenobi returned to his ship, instructing his [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R4-G9/Legends|R4-G9]] to fly his ship away and relay his attack plan to [[Clone Commander/Legends|Clone Commander]] [[Cody/Legends|Cody]]. As they left the landing platform, Fay asked Medon if the Jedi was bringing additional warriors, and the administrator responded that Kenobi had not said so.<ref name="ROTS" />

===Battle of Utapau===
{{Quote|Is he bringing additional warriors?''"<br />"''He didn't say.|Lampay Fay and Tion Medon, after the latter's conversation with Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
[[File:Occupation-of-Utapau.png|thumb|left|350px|Members of the Utapaun resistance were arrested (pictured) by clone troopers, Tion Medon among them.]]
Medon met with a MagnaGuard on an observation deck, and the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] demanded to know the Jedi's name. The Pau'an replied that he had not shared that information, lying that Kenobi had only wanted fuel.<ref name="Foe">''[[Obi-Wan's Foe]]''</ref> Medon passed on Kenobi's message to the resistance,<ref name="Databank" /> recalled the planet's hidden starfighters,<ref name="Cross Sections" /> and anxiously awaited a signal for the [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|attack]] to begin.<ref name="Databank" /> When the battle commenced, Medon placed the Utapaun military in the service<ref name="CSWE" /> of the two [[Brigade/Legends|brigades]] of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]], with Utai soldiers augmenting the Republic forces.<ref name="Databank" />

Kenobi defeated Grievous in single combat, although the battle against the Droid Army continued.<ref name="ROTS" /> Kenobi conferred with Medon at some point while the battle was ongoing.<ref name="Ultimate Missions" /> Victory for Utapau's inhabitants would be short-lived.<ref name="Databank" /> On the orders of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], secretly the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Sidious, the Republic's [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] [[Order 66/Legends|turned on]] Kenobi<ref name="ROTS" /> and placed Utapau under martial law<ref name="Utapau databank" /> in the name of Palpatine's new [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="Insider 90">{{InsiderCite|90|Aliens of Episode III}}</ref> Medon's reputation for resourcefulness meant that he was among the first Pau'ans to be [[Prisoner/Legends|imprisoned]],<ref name="CSWE" /> along with other members of the Utapaun resistance.<ref name="Databank" /> Medon and his successors initially answered to an Imperial [[Moff/Legends|Moff]], and and then to members of the Human [[Fey family]].<ref name="TEA" /> His fate after the Imperial takeover was unknown.<ref name="Fact File" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|There's no war here, unless you brought it with you.|Tion Medon, attempting to obscure his knowledge of the Separatist presence to Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
[[File:Pauan_ROTSVD.png|thumb|right|250px|Tion Medon had an imposing appearance, but was actually friendly and peaceable.]]
Despite his fearsome appearance to those unfamiliar with him,<ref name="Fact File" /> Medon had an aristocratic,<ref name="Databank" /> friendly,<ref name="Foe" /> and gentle temperament and longed for peace.<ref name="Databank" /> The administrator was accommodating, clear-thinking, and able to recognize troubling situations when he witnessed them while brave enough to act on them.<ref name="Galactic Files">{{Topps|set=2012 Topps Star Wars Galactic Files Series 1|cardname=Tion Medon (Port Administrator)|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/73989/cid/5329718/2012-Topps-Star-Wars:-Galactic-Files-89-Tion-Medon}}</ref> He was devoted to his people and willing to do anything necessary to ensure their safety.<ref name="Ultimate Missions" /> Amidst the Clone Wars, Medon remained loyal to the Republic in spite of Utapau's neutrality,<ref name="CSWE" /> and wanted to keep his people and planet safe.<ref name="Fact File" /> He was horrified to witness the deaths of the Utapau Committee members<ref name="ROTS dictionary" /> and was in a state of constant fear under the Separatist occupation.<ref name="ROTS novel" /> Although he was agreeable to Grievous's demands,<ref name="Reversal" /> Medon supported the resistance movement against the Separatists and coordinated their alliance with the Republic during the Battle of Utapau.<ref name="CSWE" /> While an honorable individual,<ref name="Fact File" /> he was also willing to lie about Kenobi's intentions to a MagnaGuard.<ref name="Foe" />

When meeting him, Kenobi saw past Medon's mask of serenity and sensed his fear rising into panic,<ref name="ROTS novel" /> suspecting that the Separatists would execute thousands of civilians if the administrator made a false move.<ref name="Junior" /> Although he was ordered to disclose Grievous's presence to lure Kenobi into a trap,<ref name="ROTS novel" /> Medon's shrewd attention to detail allowed him to provide accurate intelligence to the Jedi concerning the Separatist forces. While this allowed the Republic forces to free Utapau,<ref name="Force Collection">{{ForceCollection|Tion Medon|star=4}}</ref> Medon's reputation for resourcefulness saw him arrested by the occupying Imperial forces afterward.<ref name="CSWE" /> Even so, Medon was proud of the stance he had taken, although he was likely bitterly disappointed at the conflict's outcome.<ref name="Fact File" /> Like all Pau'ans, Medon preferred darkness to sunlight and consumed raw [[Foodstuff/Legends|meat]].<ref name="ROTS dictionary" />

Medon spoke [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]] with an accent.<ref name="ROTS novel" /> As a Pau'an, he had lined [[Color/Legends|gray]] skin&mdash;the color of which was caused by a lack of exposure to sunlight,<ref name="H2H" /> and the skin around his deep black [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] was red.<ref name="Fact File" /> Medon stood at an imposing height of 2.06 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] (6 [[Foot|feet]], 7 inches)<ref name="SWCE" /> and weighed 80 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]].<ref name="H2H" /> His narrow, [[Rat/Legends|ratlike]] [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]] gave him a frightening smile.<ref name="Ultimate Missions" />

==Skills and abilities==
Medon's long [[Limb/Legends|arms]] had a wide reach, with which he could deliver a backhanded slap.<ref name="H2H" /> His ingenuity was well-known, which led to his arrest by occupying Imperial soldiers after the Battle of Utapau.<ref name="CSWE" /> Medon could read and write in both Galactic Basic Standard and Utapese, in addition to speaking both languages alongside [[Durese/Legends|Durese]]<ref name="Ultimate Missions" /> and [[Utai (language)|Utai]].<ref name="ROTS" />

==Equipment==
During the Clone Wars, Medon wore his official administrator's uniform,<ref name="Ultimate Missions" /> consisting of elaborate red floor-length [[Clothing/Legends|robes]]&mdash;a recent fashion trend&mdash;along with a wide belt that supported his bony frame. The front of his robes below his waist had a cascading design of angled metal strips, which had its origins in the Pau'an relocation to Utapau. Medon's robes had a wide lapel collar that extended up to the sides of his head<ref name="ROTS dictionary" /> and covered his [[Ear/Legends|ear-disks]],<ref name="ROTS novel" /> and his sleeves stretched down to his hands. He also carried the ornate [[port master's walking stick]], which was fashioned from an exotic alloy,<ref name="ROTS dictionary" /> and the Pau'an could wield both an [[HB-9 rifle|HB-9]] [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]]<ref name="Toy">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (toy line)|pack=Sneak Preview #2: Tion Medon|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/rotssneaktionmedon.asp}}</ref> and a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]]. He also carried a [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]].<ref name="Ultimate Missions" />

==Behind the scenes==
===''Revenge of the Sith'' production===
====Development and casting====
{{Quote|I'm also very happy that we're using Bruce Spence. He's been in absolutely everything you can think of made in Australia! He has the most fantastic face, you know it's impossibly long and thin and very, very gaunt. He kind of looks like an Utapauan before anything's been done to him actually, apart from the grooves that we added. So what I wanted to do was make sure that he came through that makeup, because I think he's got a fantastic face and absolutely is the perfect person for this role.|Creature shop supervisor Dave Elsey, on Bruce Spence's casting as Tion Medon|<ref name="Alien Sophistication">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iii/bts/profile/f20050623/index.html|text=Alien Sophistication: Bruce Spence as Tion Medon}}</ref>}}
[[File:Bruce_Spence_headshot.png|thumb|right|250px|Bruce Spence was cast as Tion Medon in ''Star Wars'' Episode III: ''Revenge of the Sith''.]]
Tion Medon was created for the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'' Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], written and directed by [[George Lucas]].<ref name="ROTS" /> The design of the Pau'an species, completed by artist [[Sang Jun Lee]], was originally intended to be used for [[Mustafarian/Legends|Mustafarians]] on the planet [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]], but the species was moved to Utapau at Lucas's request.<ref name="Insider 90" /> The storyboards for Medon's scenes were completed by [[Derek Thompson]].<ref name="Storyboards">''[[Star Wars Storyboards: The Prequel Trilogy]]''</ref> It was initially unclear to the film's crew whether Medon would be created using practical makeup or computer-generated effects,<ref name="Databank" /> with part of the consideration towards computer-generation being given due to concerns about finding actors of an appropriate height and narrow frame.<ref name="Complete Saga Tion Medon">"Tion Medon costume featurette" &mdash; ''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''</ref> The Pau'ans were created using both methods, with the character of Tion Medon designed to utilize an actor wearing makeup.<ref name="Databank" />

[[Wikipedia:Australian people|Australian]] actor [[Bruce Spence]] was asked to audition for the role initially,<ref name="Interview 2010">{{WebCite|url=https://starwarsinterviews.com/prequel-trilogy/episode-iii-revenge-of-the-sith/bruce-spence-tion-medon|text=Bruce Spence (Tion Medon)|author=[[Dennis Pellegrom]]|date=2010-02|work=[[Star Wars Interviews]]|archivedate=20220930155038}}</ref> and was ultimately cast as Medon, which he described as "fortuitous" given that he happened to be available when offered the role after completing filming on the [[2003]] film [[Wikipedia:Peter Pan (2003 film)|''Peter Pan'']].<ref name="Homing Beacon">{{HBCite|89}}</ref> His casting was announced in an article published on [[StarWars.com]] on [[June 18]], 2003, which only identified Spence as playing a "helpful alien."<ref name="Announcement">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iii/bts/production/news20030618.html|text=Spence Joins Ep III Cast}}</ref> Costume designer [[Trisha Biggar]] felt that Spence's height worked appropriately for the character, and creature shop supervisor [[Dave Elsey]] was elated to work with Spence, believing his gaunt features made him look uniquely Pau'an even without makeup.<ref name="Alien Sophistication" />

[[File:Tion_Medon_sculpture.png|thumb|left|300px|Bruce Spence (left) and creature shop supervisor Dave Elsey look upon an early sculpture for Medon]]
Spence was initially only given basic details about his role in the film but considered the opportunity to participate in a ''Star Wars'' film fortunate. His casting gave him the distinction of appearing in the third entry of each major genre trilogy in production at the time, having appeared as the [[W:c:lotr:Mouth of Sauron|Mouth of Sauron]] in [[Wikipedia:The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King|''The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King'']] and as [[W:c:matrix:The Trainman|The Trainman]] in [[Wikipedia:The Matrix Revolutions|''The Matrix Revolutions'']]. The actor considered his ''Star Wars'' role as the least substantive of the three, while expressing gratitude for the offer.<ref name="Homing Beacon" /> Spence's casting also influenced the casting of Lampay Fay and Zyn Javeb, as the filmmakers wanted tall actors who resembled Spence's physique. Fellow Australian [[Goran Kleut]] was cast as Fay, and was particularly happy to work with Spence, whom he regarded as a legend.<ref name="Goran Kleut Interview">{{WebCite|url=https://starwarsinterviews.com/prequel-trilogy/episode-iii-revenge-of-the-sith/goran-kleut-lampay-fay|text=Goran Kleut (Lampa Fay)|author=[[Dennis Pellegrom]]|date=2010-09|work=[[Star Wars Interviews]]|archivedate=20220930161253|nolive=1}}</ref>

====Design and makeup====
{{Quote|There's sort of decorative metal pieces attached to the costumes. They're sort of a mixture of some Aztec design and a sort of 1920s design.|Costume designer Trisha Briggar, on Tion Medon's wardrobe|<ref name="Complete Saga Tion Medon" />}}
[[File:Bruce_Spence_mask.png|thumb|right|300px|Bruce Spence being fitted with the mask for Tion Medon for a makeup test]]
The lines in Medon's skin were added at Lucas's suggestion and were influenced by an [[Wikipedia:Culture of Africa|African]] sculpture<ref name="Alien Sophistication" /> and ritualistic tribal scarring, although artist [[Robert E. Barnes]] believed they were initially intended by Lucas to be colored lines like tattoos.<ref name="Insider 90" /> According to Biggar, Medon's costume mixed [[Wikipedia:Aztecs|Aztec]] clothing design and [[1920s]] aesthetics.<ref name="Complete Saga Tion Medon" /> Spence compared the costume to the vestments worn by religious priests.<ref name="Interview 2010" />

The makeup process for Medon involved taking casts of Spence's hands, which formed the basis of gloves the actor wore to represent Pau'an hands. He also wore a mask covering his whole face, aside from his eyes and nose, which were decorated with makeup.<ref name="Creatures">{{SWYouTube|krNvSGdN2Wg|The Creatures of Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith|sw_url=video/the-creatures-of-episode-iii}}</ref> Spence spent hours in makeup chairs<ref name="Insider 90" /> and completed multiple makeup and costume tests,<ref name="Making">''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref> including the creation of a [[Wikipedia:Lifecasting|lifecast]] of his body by the film's creature department by [[July 10]], 2003.<ref name="Homing Beacon" /> The lifecasting process involved having Spence's head covered from the neck upwards and covered in a pink goo and plaster with straws placed in the actor's nose to allow him to breathe while the plaster set. Spence appreciated that film prosthetics had evolved to the point that his expressions could come through, compared to previous versions that were more like static masks.<ref name="Interview 2010" /> He felt the makeup process allowed him to develop the character as he explored the possible movements of the costume, including mannerisms and twitches.<ref name="Making" />

The character's makeup also involved black contact lenses and prosthetic teeth.<ref name="SW Chronicles">''[[Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels]]''</ref> Spence found help in exploring the character through collaborating with the makeup team and Lucas. During a makeup test, Spence suggested removing the character's bottom row of prosthetic teeth, which he and Elsey agreed was an improved look for the character;<ref name="Creatures" /> this was included in the character's film appearance.<ref name="ROTS" /> By the actor's own recollection, the makeup for Medon took around four and a half hours to apply<ref name="YouTube interview">{{YouTube|video=EChz5yaRlZY|text=Tion Medon Interview with BRUCE SPENCE (2020) - Star Wars 100 Interviews|channel=@StarWars100Interviews|name=Star Wars 100 Interviews|date=2020-10-24}}</ref> and an hour to remove. Spence did not recommend the makeup process for anyone with [[Wikipedia:Claustrophobia|claustrophobia]], but he loved the finished result nonetheless.<ref name="Interview 2010" />

====Portrayal and filming====
{{Quote|I know it sounds sort of convoluted but I thought of things like the wisdom of a gorilla. Often when you look into an old gorilla you see these black piercing eyes. And even though they might be huge animals that could crush you to death to pieces, there's wonderful tenderness and an accumulated wisdom or something in that that I know is primitive but there's something there. And I thought there was also an element of that in Medon's eyes.|Bruce Spence|<ref name="Alien Sophistication" />}}
Spence took Medon's design into account when portraying the character, feeling that the character's dark eyes reminded him of the wisdom and tenderness of a [[Wikipedia:Gorilla|gorilla]] that might be present behind the character's imposing appearance.<ref name="Creatures" /> He appreciated that Medon's appearance could be seen as primitive and cruel but that his character was actually the opposite, interpreting it as a reminder that appearances can be deceiving.<ref name="Interview 2010" /> He also found the costume design helpful in defining the character's regal nature, leading to him presenting the character as though he carried a religious significance. Knowing Medon was an elderly character, Spence believed that his costume had been accumulated over a long period of time, evolving from past Utapaun administrators,<ref name="Alien Sophistication" /> with even small accessories carrying cultural significance.<ref name="Complete Saga Expanding Designs">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/me3/1.html|series=Making Episode III Webdocs|text=Two Worlds, One Movie}} &mdash; ''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''</ref> The actor viewed Medon as a revered elder statesman, believing that he would have felt slightly superior to the still-young Kenobi.<ref name="Insider 90" /> Lucas explained to Spence that Medon spoke in sophisticated tones, leading the actor to portray him with an [[Wikipedia:English people|English]] accent instead of his natural [[Wikipedia:Australian English phonology|Australian]] one.<ref name="Alien Sophistication" />

[[File:Tion_Medon_BTS.png|thumb|left|300px|Bruce Spence in costume alongside George Lucas (center) during filming]]
The scene of Medon's meeting with Kenobi was filmed over multiple takes on [[August 20]], 2003, at Stage 1 of [[Fox Studios, Sydney]].<ref name="Making" /> Spence described feeling so comfortable with the makeup and costume by that point that he came to forget he was even wearing them.<ref name="Insider 90" /> He felt the filming of the scene went smoothly and enjoyed working with Lucas,<ref name="YouTube interview" /> feeling that they were both in agreement about how the character should be portrayed. Spence also found [[Ewan McGregor]], who played Kenobi, to be a relaxed and generous actor, resulting in an easy filming process.<ref name="Interview 2010" /> He noted that he spent significantly more time preparing the makeup for the character than actually filming his scene.<ref name="YouTube interview" /> The other Pau'an actors in the same scene only wore slip-on masks, as they were not required to have the same level of precision as Medon.<ref name="Utapaun databank" /> A scene was filmed as a [[Wikipedia:Pick-up (filmmaking)|pick-up]] shot set in a golden room<ref name="Goran Kleut Interview" /> involving Medon, a MagnaGuard,<ref name="Illustrated">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay'']]</ref> and Fay,<ref name="Goran Kleut Interview" /> in which Medon is asked about Kenobi's name, and responds with the line "He didn't say."<ref name="Illustrated" /> The scene was not used in the finished film, instead Medon's line was dubbed at the end of the scene on the landing platform,<ref name="Goran Kleut Interview" /> recontextualised to be about Kenobi's additional warriors.<ref name="ROTS" />

Biggar was happy with the way Spence got into character through the costume, feeling as though he made himself taller and narrower.<ref name="Complete Saga Expanding Designs" /> Lucas described himself as a fan of Medon's character, appreciating how the film's crew created him practically with makeup and costume design. Producer [[Rick McCallum]] praised the understanding of the character that Spence showed upon his arrival on set, and how his performance was able to imply the culture of the Utapaun people.<ref name="ROTS commentary">{{Film|III}} audio commentary with [[George Lucas]], [[Rick McCallum]], [[Rob Coleman]], [[John Knoll]], and [[Roger Guyett]]</ref> In a later interview, Spence stated that he would be enthusiastic to hypothetically reprise his role for the television series ''[[Star Wars: Underworld]]'', which was under development at the time<ref name="YouTube interview" /> but never filmed.<ref name="Underworld">{{SW|url=news/10-things-you-should-know-about-saw-gerrera-from-the-clone-wars|text=10 Things You Should Know About Saw Gerrera from ''The Clone Wars''}}</ref>

===Appearances and continuity===
====First appearances====
Tion Medon was first depicted and identified in behind-the-scenes photographs included in the [[Prequel Update]]<ref name="Insider 77 PU">{{InsiderCite|77|Prequel Update}}</ref> and [[Best of Hyperspace]] sections of the [[Star Wars Insider 77|seventy-seventh issue]] of the magazine ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'',<ref name="Insider 77 BOH">{{InsiderCite|77|Best of Hyperspace}}</ref> released on [[July 22]], 2004 to subscribers and on newsstands on [[August 3]] that year.<ref name="Insider date">{{SWArchive|url=community/fanclub/mag/news20040713.html|text=Top Ten Trilogy Moments in ''Insider'' #77}}</ref> The character's visage was also used to promote exclusive production photos from the film available at [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club]], an online subscription service.<ref name="EP III Hub">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iii/bts/production/news20020508.html|text=Stars talk ''Clones'' and Ep III}}</ref> Medon made his first narrative appearance in ''[[Reversal of Fortune]]'', a Hyperspace-exclusive webstrip written by [[Paul Ens]], illustrated by [[Tom Hodges]],<ref name="Reversal" /> and released from [[October]] 2004 to [[June]] 2005.<ref name="Reversal date">{{SWArchive|url=hyperspace/about/news/news20050729.html|text=Prepare to Take Evasive Action}}</ref>

Prior to the film's premiere on [[May 19]], [[2005]],<ref name="Chronicles">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> Medon appeared in the [[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith 2|second issue]] of the film's [[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (comic series)|comic adaptation]] written by [[Christopher Cerasi]] under the pseudonym Miles Lane,<ref name="Epic Collection">''[[Star Wars Legends Epic Collection: The Clone Wars Vol. 4]]''</ref> illustrated by [[Douglas Wheatley]], and published by [[Dark Horse Comics]]<ref name="Comic">[[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith 2|''Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith'' 2]]</ref> on [[March 23]], 2005,<ref name="Comic date">{{DarkHorse|url=Comics/13-196/Star-Wars-Episode-III----Revenge-of-the-Sith-2|text=Star Wars: Episode III &mdash; Revenge of the Sith #2}}</ref> in which he meets Kenobi on the landing platform without his entourage present.<ref name="Comic" />

====Alternate scenes and continuity errors====
{{Quote|I told you, all he wanted was fuel.''"<br />"''What was his name?''"<br />"''He didn't say.|Tion Medon and a MagnaGuard, in an unused scene from ''Revenge of the Sith'' that appeared in some adaptations|<ref name="Illustrated" />}}
[[File:Pauan.png|thumb|right|300px|The scene of Medon's meeting with Kenobi has been depicted with small differences across numerous sources.]]
[[Matthew Stover]]'s [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|novelization]] of ''Revenge of the Sith'', published on [[April 2]], 2005,<ref name="Novel date">{{RandomHouseOld|url=author/results.pperl?authorid=30059|text=Matthew Woodring Stover}}</ref> contains an extended version of Medon and Kenobi's interaction with dialogue not included in the film. Medon introduces himself to Kenobi and reveals that he was ordered to inform Kenobi of Grievous's presence as part of a trap. In response, Kenobi orders R4-G9 to inform [[Jedi command/Legends|Jedi command]] that he is about to attack Grievous. He then turns to Medon and instructs him to tell the Separatists that he only wanted to refuel and make contact with [[Republic Intelligence/Legends|Republic Intelligence]]. Medon then asks for Kenobi's true intentions, and the Jedi adds that Utapau's warriors need to be ready for battle,<ref name="ROTS novel" /> as in the film.<ref name="ROTS" /> 

The film's [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay|illustrated screenplay]] and the ''[[Jedi Readers]]'' children's book ''[[Obi-Wan's Foe]]'', both published on April 2,<ref name="Illustrated date">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iii/release/publishing/news20050308.html|text=Episode III eBooks On Their Way}}</ref><ref name="Obi-Wan Amazon">{{RandomHouseOld|url=catalog/display.pperl?isbn=037580000X|text=Obi-Wan's Foe}}</ref> both include<ref name="Illustrated" /><ref name="Foe" />  the unused scene<ref name="Goran Kleut Interview" /> where Medon meets with a MagnaGuard and states that the Jedi only wanted fuel and did not provide his name.<ref name="Illustrated" /><ref name="Foe" /> 

Another Pau'an port administrator sharing Medon's surname, [[Telan Medon]], appeared in the [[Legacy (2006) 49|forty-ninth issue]] of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series ''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]'', which was written by [[John Ostrander]], penciled by [[Jan Duursema]],<ref name="Legacy">[[Legacy (2006) 49|''Legacy'' (2006) 49]]</ref> and released on [[June 30]], [[2010]].<ref name="Legacy date">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54421/star_wars_legacy_2006_49|text=Star Wars: Legacy (2006) #49}}</ref>

The [[The Official Star Wars Fact File Part 37|thirty-seventh issue]] of the [[The Official Star Wars Fact File (2014)|revised run]] of ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]'', published on [[September 17]], [[2014]]<ref name="FF37 date">{{FactFile2014Dates|37}}</ref> stated that Tion Medon had unified the cities of Utapau,<ref name="Fact File 37">{{FactFile2014|37|UTA 1-6|Utapau}}</ref> when previous sources had established that his ancestor Timon Medon had done so instead,<ref name="Utapaun databank" /><ref name="ROTS dictionary" /> including the [[The Official Star Wars Fact File Part 9|ninth issue]] of the Fact File<ref name="Fact File" /> which was published on [[March 5]], 2014.<ref name="Fact File 9 Date">{{FactFile2014Dates|9}}</ref>

====Non-canonical appearances====
{{Quote|We do have some lovely pre-owned Imperial ships from the old days you might like. This baby belonged to General Grievous. Only drove it on weekends.|Tion Medon, to Luke Skywalker and his companions|<ref name="Race">{{YodaChronicles|Race for the Holocrons}}</ref>}}
The [[2011]] young readers book ''[[Star Wars: Head-to-Head Tag Teams]]'', written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]], places Medon in a scenario where he is allied with the [[Umbaran/Legends|Umbaran]] Republic [[Agent/Legends|agent]] [[Sly Moore/Legends|Sly Moore]] and the [[Kubaz/Legends|Kubaz]] [[Spy/Legends|spy]] [[Garindan/Legends|Garindan]] against the [[Skakoan/Legends|Skakoan]] [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] [[Foreman/Legends|Foreman]] [[Wat Tambor/Legends|Wat Tambor]], the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Lott Dod/Legends|Lott Dod]], and the [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] war criminal [[Kardue'sai'Malloc/Legends|Labria]]. The scenario takes place in the [[Grand Convocation Chamber]] on<ref name="H2H" /> the Republic capital planet<ref name="TEA" /> [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. The book states that Medon would instinctively take a leadership role for his team during the conflict, which would work effectively in combination with Moore's mental abilities and Garindan's stealth prowess. The expert's pick section of the book states that Tambor would use a prototype [[Weapon/Legends|weapon]] to attack Moore and disrupt her abilities, giving his team the advantage.<ref name="H2H" />

Medon, voiced by [[Trevor Devall]], appears in "[[Race for the Holocrons]]," the fifth episode of the [[Canon|non-canonical]] [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] short film series ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Yoda Chronicles]]'',<ref name="Race" /> which aired on [[Disney XD]] on [[June 15]], 2014.<ref name="Race date">{{SWYouTube|oCEEV4ftR_w|LEGO Star Wars: The New Yoda Chronicles "Race for the Holocrons" Clip}}</ref> Following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Jedi Master [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] and the [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]] of Kenobi sent [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] on a mission to retrieve [[Holocron/Legends|holocrons]] to support his journey to become a Jedi.<ref name="Escape">{{YodaChronicles|Escape from the Jedi Temple}}</ref> Led by the Force, Skywalker and his companions, [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and the droids [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], arrived on Utapau and met with Medon on a high level inside one of Utapau's sinkholes. When the Jedi hopefully inquired about the holocrons, Medon initially misheard Skywalker, who repeated the name of the holocrons again, and Medon initially appeared to recognize the name before revealing that he had never heard of them.<ref name="Race" />

[[File:Lego_Tion_Medon.png|thumb|right|300px|Tion Medon and a crowd of Utai cheer after Luke Skywalker's feat.]]
Ignoring Skywalker's disappointment, Medon directed his attention to several second-hand pre-Imperial vehicles available for purchase, including a [[Star Courier/Legends|Star Courier]], a [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter/Legends|V-wing starfighter]], a [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|vulture droid]], a Jedi interceptor, an [[SS-54 assault ship/Legends|SS-54 assault ship]], and a [[Tsmeu-6 personal wheel bike]]. Medon highlighted the wheel bike, stating that it had belonged to Grievous, who had only used it on weekends. Organa declined Medon's offer, and shortly afterward, Skywalker kicked a rock in frustration, hitting a wild [[Varactyl/Legends|varactyl]] that attacked Skywalker and his companions, knocking Organa and the droids into the sinkhole.<ref name="Race" />

Skywalker leapt in after them and used the Force to quickly assemble a bridge from falling debris, saving his friends while the varactyl continued plummeting. When the creature began climbing back up the sinkhole, Skywalker used the Force to launch his group back onto the level where Medon stood, now accompanied by a crowd of Utai. Medon and the crowd cheered at Skywalker's feat, but Organa quickly noticed that the varactyl was still pursuing them, and Skywalker asked Medon for a test drive of the V-wing starfighter while running towards it. Medon asked for Skywalker's driver's license, but he responded that there was no time. Medon and the Utai watched as the varactyl climbed onto their level and leapt onto the starfighter, but Skywalker was able to knock it down into the sinkhole and fly offworld to search for the holocrons on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="Race" />
